comment: <summary>
One-click "imported VRM → drop-in NPC model" builder. Takes a VRM model that
UniVRM already imported (the generated prefab/GameObject) plus an npcId, and emits
<c>Assets/Resources/CharacterModels/<npcId>.prefab</c> — exactly the path
<c>NPCController.TrySwapModel</c> auto-loads, so the NPC's gray capsule is replaced
at runtime with zero further wiring.
Deliberately references NO UniVRM types (compiles with or without UniVRM in the
project). It only touches generic Unity components:
• optional idle AnimatorController so the Humanoid model doesn't stand in T-pose;
• optional material conversion MToon → ChronoTraveler/ToonOutline (fixes the URP
"pink material" issue AND matches the game's cel-shaded look), with a plain
URP/Lit fallback.
Static NPCs (the project's minimum bar) just need the mesh standing; the protagonist
keeps its own rigged setup and does NOT go through this tool.
</summary>
ToonOutline is a Built-in-RP shader → magenta in URP
metres — AI meshes export unit-normalised, scale to human height
Hunyuan front-view exports face -Z; NPCController turns +Z to the player, so flip 180° to show the front
Candidate shader-property names across MToon 0.x / MToon10 / URP for the base
texture and base colour — we copy whichever the source material actually exposes.
Work on a throwaway instance so we never mutate the source import.
Make it an independent object (not linked to the source prefab) so the saved
NPC prefab owns its own converted materials / controller.
Wrap in a clean root whose origin = feet-centre, facing +Z, scaled to human
height. NPCController.TrySwapModel then drops this root at the capsule floor and
the feet land on the ground regardless of the mesh's own pivot.
re-centre: feet-centre → root origin
Combined world-space AABB of all child renderers (false if the object has none).
mainTexture maps to the shader's main-tex tag if present; fall back to scanning.
<summary>
Bakes the finale boss trueform from the Hunyuan 3D Studio FBX set (rigged + skinned +
one animation per file) into a game-ready prefab:
Assets/Art/Characters/Finale/boss_{idle,attack,hitdown,leap}.fbx
→ configure importers (Generic rig, looping idle, extracted textures)
→ URP/Lit materials (FBX Standard materials render magenta under URP)
→ AnimatorController (Idle default-loop; attack/hit/leap triggers)
→ Resources/CharacterModels/finale_boss_trueform.prefab (10m tall, grounded, +Z facing)
Used by the two-act finale rework: the pinned, EMBODIED boss standing on the platform.
Idempotent — re-run after replacing any FBX.
</summary>
spec: an 8-12m embodied colossus on the platform
---- 1) importer pass: Generic rig, loop the idle, pull embedded textures ----
one texture set serves all four (same model)
---- 2) animator: Idle loops by default; the rest fire on triggers, then return ----
---- 3) prefab: idle FBX as the body, URP materials, 10m grounded, +Z facing ----
Hunyuan exports face -Z (NPC-pipeline finding) — flip to +Z.
Normalize: renderer bounds → 10m tall, feet on y=0, centred on origin.
<summary>FBX Standard materials → URP/Lit with the same base texture (magenta fix).</summary>
<summary>
Bakes the decimated Xuanji OBJ (output of tools/decimate_xuanji.py) into
<c>Resources/CharacterModels/xuanji.prefab</c> — the drop-in 3D body that
CompanionController prefers over its 2D sprite fallback. Floating-mascot
specifics vs NPCModelSetupTool: the pivot is the renderer-bounds CENTRE
(the body hangs on a hover anchor — no feet, no ground) and normalisation
is by body LENGTH (longest horizontal axis; the pose is a curled lying fox),
not by height.
</summary>
metres along the longest axis (Paimon-scale)
The GLB's orientation node is lost in the OBJ conversion: the raw mesh lies face-UP
(supine, +Y). Pitch +90 stands the curled-fox "disc" upright with the face on +Z —
the medallion view the runtime then billboards at the camera. (Round 2: -90/180 put
her head-down; +90/0 keeps the face forward and flips the head axis up.)
pivot = bounds centre (hover anchor)
Fixed path so re-running the menu overwrites instead of piling up xuanji_body_1.mat.
<summary>
Drops a model so its ANIMATED silhouette stands on the ground. The finale trueform
was baked feet-at-origin from the FBX bind pose, but the Animator's idle pose shifts
the skeleton and the boss hovered (user reports ×2 — the first attempt read
Renderer.bounds, which for a SkinnedMeshRenderer is the STATIC import-time bind-pose
box moved by the root bone, not the animated pose; the measured offset came out ~0
and the fix was a no-op, Q30). Ground truth instead: BakeMesh snapshots the current
skinned vertices and the lowest vertex is the real animated foot line. One-shot after
the Animator settles; works for any future rigged swap-in.
</summary>
Animator has applied the idle pose by now
The idle loop BOBS: a single-frame sample lands mid-bob and the feet still
hover for the rest of the cycle (user report, residual ~0.1-0.2). Sample the
lowest vertex across ~one loop and snap to the global minimum.
Ground under the model, skipping our own hierarchy (the trigger root carries
the interact/blocker sphere, which a plain raycast would hit first).
nothing below — leave as-is
Empirical correction + settle: the stable reading falls ~0.2 short of the true
hover (bracketed by the two play-tested mappings above), and a colossus should
press slightly into its footing anyway. 0.3 lands within ±0.1 of flush —
grazing or faintly embedded, both read as grounded on a 10 m stone giant.
<summary>World-space lowest visible point of the ANIMATED model. Skinned meshes
are baked (their .bounds lie about the pose); static meshes use renderer bounds.</summary>
Hunyuan rigs carry bone/unit scaling that poisons BOTH BakeMesh scale
interpretations, in opposite directions — measured on this rig:
useScale:true + rot/pos map   → 0.68  (short: ~0.2 hover remained)
useScale:false + localToWorld → 2.29  (far: sank ~1.5 into the floor)
True hover bracketed at ≈0.9. Keep the STABLE reading (0.72/0.68 across
runs) and fold the empirically-derived shortfall into Settle below.
<summary>
The finale's stage turn: after Xuanji pins the Unwritten into certain form, the
formless colossus looming beyond the platform dissolves and the EMBODIED trueform
(Hunyuan-baked prefab, idle-looping) stands on the platform as a walk-up duel.
Pure runtime transform of the scene's existing finale BattleTrigger — its serialized
loadout/enemy references are reused, so no scene rebuild and no Resources copies of
the _Content assets are needed. Idempotent: the Trueform child marks "already done".
</summary>
<summary>Centre-stage on the starstone platform (top at y=0), far enough from the
spawn (z=-9) to walk toward, facing it. The 10m trueform reads as a duelist here,
not the 450m overseer act 1 fought.</summary>
<summary>Swap the colossus for the embodied trueform. Returns false if already
embodied. Safe to call right after map entry (behind the fade) or after the
awakening cutscene (the burst covers the swap).</summary>
The colossus dissolves where it loomed (bone-white, its own colourlessness).
Strip the formless look: visual components FIRST (their Update loops drive the
generated children), then every generated child, then the gray-box sphere itself.
Pinned into certain form: person-scale trigger standing on the platform,
facing the spawn. The sphere collider doubles as body blocker + E-interact range.
Root stays identity: the baked prefab already carries the 180° model flip, and
an extra root flip cancelled it — the trueform stood with its back to the
arriving player (user play report).
The prefab was normalized feet-at-origin from the BIND pose; the idle
animation shifts the skeleton and the boss hovered (user report).
GroundSnap measures the animated silhouette and drops it onto the platform.
Missing-art tolerance: keep the sphere as act 2's body, but leave the
idempotence marker so the swap doesn't re-run every entry.
Billboard, PropVisuals
<summary>
Xuanji's "body" — follows the player during exploration. Prefers the baked 3D model
(Resources/CharacterModels/xuanji — a curled fox lying on starlight, Paimon-style hover)
and falls back to the original 2D billboard sprite when the prefab is absent, so the
game runs unchanged before the asset lands. Self-boots + DDOL; hides outside
<see cref="GameState.Exploring"/> (battle uses the bottom-left speaker instead).
A dumb view: the CompanionDirector calls <see cref="SetMood"/> — on the 3D path a
non-Idle mood pops a small overhead bubble (the static mesh has no expressions).
</summary>
2D fallback body (null when the 3D model is in use)
3D body root (null on the 2D fallback path)
overhead emotion bubble (3D path only)
Time.time after which the bubble fades out
smoothed forward-lean while the player moves
2D sprite: world-units tall, regardless of PPU
3D bubble: world-units tall
deterministic per-instance phase
Asset-missing immunity: identical to the pre-3D behaviour.
<summary>The fox lies on a faint pool of drifting gold/ice-blue star motes —
the literal reading of "a little fox lying on starlight". Kept dim on purpose:
the companion must never outshine the player or the scene.</summary>
soft gold
ice blue
Unity requires all three velocity axes to share one curve MODE ("Particle
Velocity curves must all be in the same mode"): setting only y to TwoConstants
left x/z in their default Constant mode. Zero-width TwoConstants ranges keep
x/z motionless while satisfying the same-mode rule.
Static mesh has no expressions — non-Idle moods pop the overhead bubble.
<summary>Scale the 2D body so it reads ~DesiredHeight tall whatever the sprite's PPU/size.</summary>
Show during free exploration (hub or era), but never at the main menu / while paused —
both freeze time, so timeScale is the robust "actually in-game" signal (works even when
a scene is play-tested directly, where SceneFlowManager.CurrentMapScene is never set).
Hover beside-and-above the player (their right shoulder), smoothed, with a gentle bob.
<summary>Programmatic life for the rig-less mesh: the curled-fox "medallion" always
faces the camera (soft billboard, matching the 2D sprite behaviour), breathes with a
slow pitch sway and leans forward while the player moves. The 2D path never gets
here (Billboard owns its rotation).</summary>
Upper bound rejects teleports (map travel writes the transform directly).

Localized: the NPC's display name is resolved by id (scene-baked npcName is the
fallback), and the prompt template comes from the UI string table.

<summary>World-state dialogue ladder: the era's people react to progress. Variants
are optional data — "<id>_post" once the era's boss has fallen (starstone
earned), "<id>_gate" when the seal loosens (memory full), "<id>_mid"
past half memory. An absent variant falls down the ladder to the base dialogue, so
everything keeps working before the content lands. Quest/journal completion always
reports the BASE id (DialogueManager strips the suffix).</summary>
Scene name → era token id (the same lowercase ids EraProgress stores).
The era map (and its NPCs) is unloaded while DialogueManager persists (DDOL).
Drop any live subscription so a dialogue ending can't invoke a destroyed NPC.
Change indicator color to show completion
<summary>
Drop-in real model for a gray-box object (e.g. the player capsule). On Start,
instantiates an explicit prefab or one from Resources/CharacterModels/<resourceId>
as a child, and hides the host's placeholder MeshRenderer. No-op if none found.
(Animator wiring for the player is asset-specific and set up when the model exists.)
</summary>
